criteria.text: Provide an obvious Add project action in the Agents tab, including when no projects or sessions exist.
criteria.test_id: add an empty project, reload, select it and create a correctly bound session without running an agent

criteria.text: Let the user provide a project name and choose a working directory using the native directory picker from #1496, with manual path entry available as an alternative.
criteria.test_id: native picker cancellation and form Escape preserve path, selection and focus without creating anything

criteria.text: Create through the existing agent-project API and preserve its directory validation and duplicate-project rules. Show understandable validation/error feedback and prevent duplicate submissions.
criteria.test_id: gateway preserves project fields, existing request auth and readable backend errors

criteria.text: After successful creation, the project appears and can be selected immediately even before it has any sessions. It remains available after refresh/relaunch.
criteria.test_id: add an empty project, reload, select it and create a correctly bound session without running an agent

criteria.text: Starting a session in the selected project uses the intended project identity and working directory; existing sessions and their grouping remain correct.
criteria.test_id: live sandbox project persists and a new session retains its exact directory and project identity

criteria.text: Canceling the form or directory picker creates nothing and preserves existing selection. The project-creation flow must not automatically run an agent, initialize instructions, switch branches, or modify files in the selected directory.
criteria.test_id: native picker cancellation and form Escape preserve path, selection and focus without creating anything

criteria.text: Keyboard access, loading/empty/error states, long names/paths, and the new project's empty-session state are usable.
criteria.test_id: picker selection supports long paths and advanced creation inherits only the chosen project context
